key_insight: Off-the-shelf large language models can automatically extract key breast oncology variables from very long, messy longitudinal charts with high agreement for several outcomes and biomarkers.
clinical_relevance: This could reduce manual chart abstraction burden in cancer research by speeding identification of recurrence, tumor markers, and treatment histories from narrative records.
method: Randomly sampled 100 patients from an institutional breast cancer cohort.
Compared four general-purpose LLMs against oncologist abstraction, genetic testing records, and selected coordinator-reviewed variables.
Used an open-source, HIPAA-compliant pipeline without fine-tuning or hand-selected documents.
evidence_signal: In the best-performing models (GPT-5 and Gemini 2.5 Pro), the pipeline reached 90%–100% concordance for recurrence and multiple biomarker variables, and it was also tested in a separate 97-patient cohort for recurrence detection.
watch_item: Results need replication across institutions and diseases, and therapy-line reconstruction was less accurate than oncologist review.
paper_title: Fully Automated Abstraction of Longitudinal Breast Oncology Records with Off-The-Shelf Large Language Models
